metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers catches three passes Sunday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers caught three passes for 33 yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wasn't able to do much of note on Sunday, finishing with just 33 yards in a narrow win over the Bengals. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be relevant moving forward, however, especially with some tough matchups coming up for Jacksonville's offense over the next two weeks.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Three catches in win
metadata.description: Meyers caught three of four targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 22-17 win against the Bengals.
metadata.analysis: Meyers finished second on the team in targets behind tight end Brenton Strange (eight), but his performance was far from noteworthy. The wide receiver has operated as a distant No. 2 option behind Parker Washington at his position this season, and Sunday's performance was his third game with 40 or fewer receiving yards over four contests.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Looking to Build Off Last Week's Big Game
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers is trending up in fantasy football. After catching just three passes through the first two weeks, Meyers exploded with seven catches, 64 yards, and one touchdown last Sunday against his old team, the New England Patriots. Parker Washington is still the top Jaguars receiver in fantasy football, but Meyers' big performance in Week 3 has cemented him as a strong WR3/flex option going forward. Meyers ranks first in the NFL in target separation against man coverage this year, and he also ranks first in quarterback rating when targeted. The underlying metrics suggest that Meyers should have a much bigger role than he has occupied this season, so we don't think that his big Week 3 was any sort of fluke. This week, he'll also benefit from a matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, whose pass defense has been nothing special. Cincinnati ranks near the middle of the league with the 15th-fewest fantasy points allowed to wide receivers in 2026.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Good to go for Week 4
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
metadata.analysis: With limited listings earlier in the week, Meyers practiced fully Friday and is fine for his normal workload against Cincinnati. Meyers was targeted a season-high eight times last Sunday against the Patriots but has just 11 targets on the season over three games. He's a low-floor WR4 for fantasy, but this game does have some shootout appeal.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) listed as limited Thursday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: As expected, Meyers remained a limited participant for another practice on Thursday. He should be good to go for Sunday's game, however, assuming he doesn't suffer any setbacks between now and then.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Stays limited in practice
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: The Jaguars have been restricting Meyers' practice activity through the four weeks of the regular season after he jammed his right thumb during a joint practice with Carolina in training camp, but the issue hasn't kept him from suiting up on gamedays. He's expected to cleared to play Sunday in Cincinnati following Friday's practice.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) limited participant Wednesday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wideout is again listed with thumb injury that left him limited at practice on Wednesday, but it's not a serious issue and shouldn't prevent him from playing in Week 4. He doesn't project to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy option at this point in the season, however.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Limited with thumb issue
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Meyers dealt with the thumb issue last week but ultimately didn't carry an injury designation into last Sunday's blowout win over the Patriots, where the veteran wideout hung a 7-64-1 receiving line on eight targets. Playing as a clear starter ahead of Brian Thomas, Meyers has 10 catches for 132 yards and two touchdowns on 11 targets through three games this season.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers leads team in receiving Sunday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers caught 7-of-8 targets for 64 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Meyers had a fantastic game against his former team on Sunday. He led the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards over the course of the afternoon and was also able to score a touchdown, which was the cherry on top. This was a good game for the veteran, but fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to put up numbers like this week-in and week-out moving forward.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers a Top Waiver Priority After His Best Game of the Season
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers caught a season-high seven passes for 64 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's blowout win over his former team, the Patriots. After a quiet start to the season in which he was targeted only three times in the first two weeks, Meyers appears to have emerged as the team's second receiver, coming up big in a game in which the defensive game plan limited Parker Washington to a season-low three catches. What was seen as one of the most wide-open receiver rooms coming into the season looks to have developed a clear hierarchy, with both Meyers and Washington holding a near-every-down role. Meanwhile, Brian Thomas Jr. has found himself in a rotation with sixth-round rookie Josh Cameron, and two-way player Travis Hunter continues to feature primarily on defense, seeing only five offensive snaps in Week 3. Meyers remains a flex-worthy play moving forward and should be viewed as a priority waiver add wherever available.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Finds paydirt in blowout win
metadata.description: Meyers caught seven of eight targets for 64 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 35-6 win over New England.
metadata.analysis: Meyers led the team in targets, most notably reeling in a 10-yard score from quarterback Trevor Lawrence in the second quarter. The touchdown was the second of the year for the wide receiver, and he has now caught 10 of 11 targets for 132 yards over three contests in 2026. Parker Washington has established himself as Lawrence's favorite target, but Meyers has found himself on equal footing with fellow wideout Brian Thomas as an unpredictable fantasy asset early in the season.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers a Deep-League Flex Against Patriots
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (thumb) practiced fully on Friday and is good to go for a Week 3 matchup with the New England Patriots. Meyers has been busy in terms of playing time to start the year but has been out-produced by both Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. He did manage to score in Week 1, but he has only had three catches through two games. The veteran receiver played 90% of the snaps in Week 2, which is promising, but playing time doesn't matter if you aren't earning targets. There is the narrative of Meyers facing one of his former teams, but that isn't enough of a boost for him to be viewed as a reliable fantasy starter. Meyers has a chance to produce more given his performance at the end of last season, but for now he shouldn't be trusted beyond deeper leagues in Week 3.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) is good to go for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
metadata.analysis: As expected, the veteran wideout's thumb injury is not a serious issue for him and he will play through it on Sunday. He will be up against his former team on Sunday, but fantasy managers still shouldn't consider him a trustworthy option in that interesting matchup.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Avoids injury designation
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Meyers quietly leads the Jaguars with an 86 percent route share, but he's been targeted on just 6 percent of his routes, taking a backseat to Parker Washington and Brian Thomas, in that order. Thomas' sloppy play in a Week 2 loss at Denver could perhaps push more volume in Meyers' direction, though that's likely to happen in any case even if his thumb injury continues to linger.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Barely Seeing the Ball in Jacksonville
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers has been on the field plenty, but the targets have almost vanished. Meyers caught both of his looks for 40 yards and a touchdown in Week 1, then saw only one target against Denver and turned it into a 28-yard catch. He still played 54 snaps and ran a team-high 29 routes in that loss. Trevor Lawrence just kept going elsewhere, with Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. combining for 20 targets. That is a rough change for Meyers after he averaged nearly seven targets per game in nine appearances with Jacksonville last season, catching 42 passes for 483 yards and three touchdowns. The thumb injury is still being managed, but Meyers has not missed a game because of it. RotoBaller has him at WR54 for Week 3 against New England. The routes are keeping him on the fantasy radar for now, but three targets in two games is nowhere near enough to trust in a lineup.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Remains limited Thursday
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) was a limited participant Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The Jaguars put a cap on Meyers' reps for the second day in a row, but head coach Liam Coen hasn't provided any indication that the wideout is at any real risk of sitting out Sunday's game against the Patriots while he continues to manage a right thumb injury that dates back to training camp. Meyers played through the thumb issue in the first two contests of the season, recording three catches for 68 yards and a touchdown on three targets.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) listed as limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran should be fine to play in Week 3, despite being limited at practice all week so far. Barring any setbacks with his recovery, he should be a full go against his former team on Sunday but still doesn't project to be a strong option from a fantasy perspective.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Limited in Wednesday's practice
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) was listed as a limited participant for Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union reports.
metadata.analysis: The veteran has been held back in practice for much of the season due to a thumb issue, but it hasn't prevented him from suiting up on Sundays. Look for the Jaguars to continue to manage Meyers' injury cautiously in practices to keep him fresh on gamedays. The wideout still looks to be on track to play Week 3 versus the Patriots.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) a limited participant Wednesday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: A thumb injury left Meyers limited at Jacksonville's first practice of the week on Wednesday. It doesn't seem likely to affect his availability for Week 3, however, and he should continue to play his usual role in a matchup against his former team, the Patriots, this week if he suffers no setbacks in his recovery.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers held to one catch in Week 2
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers caught his lone target for a 28-yard gain in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Meyers didn't record his lone catch of the game until the fourth quarter as he took a backseat to both Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. Meyers has now caught all three of his targets for 68 yards and a touchdown through two games this season. He will be a flex consideration heading into Week 3 against the Patriots.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Draws one target in Week 2
metadata.description: Meyers secured his only target for 28 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Broncos.
metadata.analysis: On a day Trevor Lawrence threw for just 189 yards on 29 attempts, Parker Washington and Brian Thomas combined to see 20 of those targets. Meyers dealt with a thumb injury during the practice week but still led all wideouts with 54 snaps against Denver, running a team-high 29 routes. Through two games, Meyers has just three catches for 68 yards and a touchdown on three targets. He's tough to get behind as anything more than a fantasy WR4 ahead of next Sunday's game against the Patriots.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
metadata.analysis: Meyers was on the injury report all week due to a lingering wrist issue, but he is going to be good to go and will play in Sunday's game against the Broncos. Fantasy managers shouldn't trust in his week-to-week consistency at this point in the season, however, especially in what projects to be a tough matchup.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers a Solid PPR Flex Option in Week 2
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited at practice all week but is good to go against the Denver Broncos in Week 2. The Jaguars' passing attack will look to continue its stellar play stemming from last season against a defense with a strong reputation. However, the Kansas City Chiefs gashed the Broncos last week in a 31-10 victory, and the Jaguars scored 34 points on the Broncos in Denver just last season. Those signs point to what could be another great offensive outing, even in a much harder matchup than the Cleveland Browns from Week 1. Meyers doesn't have the upside of a Brian Thomas Jr. or Parker Washington, but he does have a decent floor, especially in PPR leagues. It is also promising that Meyers led Jaguars receivers in Week 1 snaps, although Thomas Jr. did miss some time in the first half with a shoulder injury. The Jaguars have a crowded room of pass catchers, but the offense does spread the ball around, meaning Meyers should be viewed as a flex option with a limited ceiling against the Broncos.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Ready for Week 2
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) was limited at Friday's practice but doesn't have an injury designation for Week 2 at Denver, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union reports.
metadata.analysis: Brian Thomas (shoulder) also avoided an injury designation despite being limited in practice throughout the week. He picked up his injury during the Week 1 win over Cleveland, whereas Meyers is listed with the same thumb injury that he played through successfully in the season opener.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Will Play in Week 2 in Denver
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited in practice all week, but he does not carry an injury designation on Friday's final injury report and will play in Week 2 on Sunday in Denver against the Broncos, per The Florida Times-Union's Ryan O'Halloran. Meyers, who was a bit of a forgotten man during the summer in training camp, caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the season-opening win over the Cleveland Browns. The 29-year-old dealt with a thumb injury late in training camp, but it was nothing serious, and he was able to play in the season opener. Now that he is officially cleared for Week 2, Meyers should be considered a WR3/4 in his second game of the 2026 season as he competes for targets with Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. In last year's 34-20 win over the Broncos in Denver in Week 16, Meyers caught four of his eight targets for 45 yards.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) limited participant Thursday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) was a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran was again a limited participant on Thursday, which was to be expected, as the team has left him limited at all of their official practices so far in the regular season. He should be good to go for Week 2 and will see more work than usual if Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) is sidelined against the Broncos.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Remains limited in practice
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Meyers emerged from preseason Week 2 with a brace on his right hand, but the nature of the injury wasn't confirmed until the Jaguars posted their first injury report of the season last week. Since then, he's been listed as limited on all five of the team's practice reports with a thumb injury, but it didn't stop him from suiting up for this past Sunday's season-opening win against the Browns, when he hauled in both targets for 40 yards and one touchdown and recorded one carry for two yards on a 65 percent snap share. If Meyers follows last week's trajectory this week, he'll enter the weekend without a designation for Sunday's contest at Denver.
